payload.name: Concrete Project Retrieval for Broad Category Questions
payload.description: When a question asks what kind/types of projects or work a person has done in a broad category, use after initial retrieval to check specificity and search for named examples without the category term.
content: When a question asks what kind of projects or work a person has done in a broad category (e.g., engineering, research, art), do not stop after the first retrieval returns generic memories that only mention the category without concrete project names or topics.

If the retrieved memories are vague about the actual project subject, run a follow-up search that omits the broad category keyword and uses the person's name plus outcome/action terms such as 'designed', 'built', 'developed', 'created', 'prototype', 'system', 'device', 'working on', or 'completed'.
Include memory kinds 'event', 'plan', 'state', and 'profile' in the follow-up, and inspect returned memories for concrete project descriptions (e.g., named products, systems, or technologies).
Stop after one additional targeted search that yields no new concrete project names; do not expand exhaustively.

solves: When a question asks what kinds or types of projects a person has worked on in a broad field (e.g., engineering, research, art), retrieval can over-anchor on the field name and return generic category-tagged memories while missing concrete project examples that actually define the types. This skill prompts the agent to verify that retrieved memories name specific projects and, when they are too vague, to run a follow-up search using the person's name and outcome/action terms without the broad category keyword.
